item.title: Nº 007 — How do birds sense magnetic fields?
item.description: A robin can feel a force you cannot. The leading explanation requires quantum mechanics operating inside a warm, wet eye.

item.title: Nº 006 — Does P equal NP?
item.description: If checking an answer is easy, is finding one easy too? A million-dollar question about the nature of difficulty itself.

item.title: Nº 005 — Why is ice slippery?
item.description: A question a child can ask, studied since Faraday, still argued in physics journals. The textbook answer you learned is mostly wrong.

item.title: Nº 004 — How did life begin?
item.description: Somewhere on the early Earth, chemistry became biology. Every laboratory attempt to repeat the trick has stalled at the same gap.

item.title: Nº 003 — Why does anesthesia work?
item.description: We have been switching human consciousness off on demand since 1846. We still cannot say what the switch is.

item.title: Nº 002 — What is dark matter?
item.description: Five independent lines of evidence say most of the matter in the universe is invisible. Fifty years of searching have not caught a single particle of it.

item.title: Nº 001 — Why do we sleep?
item.description: Every animal with a nervous system does it. It is dangerous, costly, and non-negotiable, and nobody knows what it is buying.
